question: During the deposition procedure, which type of state conversion will take place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gaseous to solid state**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deposition is a phase transition in which gas transforms directly into solid without passing through the liquid phase.
 
• This process is the opposite of sublimation, where a solid changes directly into a gas.
 
• Common examples of deposition include the formation of frost on cold surfaces and the creation of snowflakes in clouds.
 
• During deposition, the molecules of the gas lose energy and slow down enough to settle into a rigid, fixed structure as a solid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation**

 
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state, without passing through the liquid state.
 
• Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) sublimates at room temperature, turning directly from a solid into carbon dioxide gas.
 
 
 
• **Condensation**
 
 
• Condensation is the process by which water vapor in the air is changed into liquid water.
 
• This process is crucial in the water cycle and is responsible for the formation of clouds.
 
 
 
• **Freezing**
 
 
• Freezing is the process where a liquid turns into a solid when its temperature is lowered below its freezing point.
 
• Water freezing into ice at 0°C (32°F) is a common example.
 
 
 
• **Melting**
 
 
• Melting is the process of a solid becoming a liquid due to an increase in temperature.
 
• Ice melting into water is a typical example of this phase transition.
